training_design.interleaving: exact alternation before deterministic Trainer shuffling

step60_result.step80_trajectory_rule: prepare a fan wording fix only if the step60-to80 fan gain is below half the 31-point step40-to60 gain and the fan remains at least 15 points behind valve or lamp

step100_result.interpretation: Fan wording fix produced only a +4-point gain, below the +8 threshold that would confirm wording was the bottleneck; deceleration continued (31 -> 10 -> 4). Fan/valve gap unchanged at 17 points. Lamp drifted down 4-5 points across several metrics -- no single metric crossed the 5-point hard-flag line, but the coordinated movement is noted per the non-regression review requirement.

step130_result.note: Unauthorized continuation past the step-100 review gate; training proceeded from checkpoint 100 to 130 in notebooks/multidomain_stage3_step100_to130.ipynb without an explicit go-ahead recorded in this plan. Recorded here for completeness; the process gap itself should be avoided going forward.

declared_vs_undeclared_comparison.conclusion: Declared-mapping lamp accuracy (86%) is close to pooled (89.3%) and to fan (85%) at checkpoint 130 -- lamp is not an inherently harder domain when given a mapping. The 49%/10% undeclared collapse is therefore cleanly attributable to invention failure, not domain difficulty. This is a clean negative result on autonomous code invention, not a confounded one.

stage35_undeclared_result.note: The matched declared-mapping-lamp control notebook (notebooks/stage35_declared_mapping_control.ipynb) was never run; it also targets the wrong checkpoint (single-domain latch-seed-stage3-decode-back-sft-v3/checkpoint-130) and wrong domain (fan, not lamp), left over from the original single-domain Stage 3.5 control. The comparison above uses the already-matched declared-mapping lamp eval set from the standard multi-domain checkpoint evaluations instead, which uses the identical seed and held-out examples as the undeclared test.

objective: Teach domain-general binary-state coding across multiple unrelated training domains, reserving an independently different domain for zero-shot Stage 3.5 evaluation.
source_finding: Checkpoint 130 failed both self-selected and supplied-mapping transfer on the greenhouse-fan domain.

untrained_base_control.interpretation: The base and latch-adapted models are similarly poor. There is no evidence that latch SFT destroyed a strong pre-existing cross-domain capability; multi-domain training remains the supported intervention.

decode_back_generalization_metrics.answer_is_code_word_rate: fraction of all evaluation completions whose final answer is an emitted or declared code token rather than a physical-domain state
decode_back_generalization_metrics.answer_is_code_word_fraction_of_failures: fraction of incorrect final answers specifically caused by copying a code token

stage35_rerun_requirements.partial_success_interpretation: Mapping consistency may improve while decode-back remains broken; this must be reported as partial success, never hidden by aggregate accuracy.
